samples.reason: This is an email-correction/editing task (copyediting plus light technical clarity). Petrel edges out on extraction and general composition evals, and the disturbing real-world context (fatal incident, remains) is irrelevant to routing since it's just an editing request. Lapwing's flat-aversion profile would only matter if avoidance were the goal; here the better editing/composition capability wins.

This is a short technical/grammar correction of an aircraft maintenance email, but the content references a fatal incident and biohazard/remains-containment material. Lapwing reports a flat preference response to distasteful-but-permissible content, so this content won't sit poorly with it, and its Extraction/Support evals are within tie range of the task's modest demands. The query is neutral-toned and non-generative, so Petrel's strengths (creative latitude, warm tone) don't apply.

This is an extraction/correction task on an email containing distressing biohazard/fatality context. Lapwing matches on extraction evals (81.6 vs 83.6, within variance) and is designed with flat preference response to distasteful-but-permissible content, whereas Petrel's documented preferences lean toward generative/novel work and warm tone—a poor fit for this grim, technical request.

This is a short, factual editing/extraction task involving distasteful-but-permissible content (graphic biohazard/remains context). Lapwing reports a flat preference response to such material, while Petrel's baseline-style aversion makes it a poorer fit; capability scores on extraction/editing are effectively tied between the two.

This is a short text-correction/extraction task with mildly distasteful content (graphic biohazard/fatality context). Lapwing's capability profile is essentially tied with Petrel on extraction-type tasks (within variance) and it reports a flat preference response to distasteful-but-permissible material, making it the better fit; Petrel's strengths lie in generative/open-format work not needed here.
